prompt: Write a recursive SQL query that returns the full management chain for employee with id = 5. Return one row per ancestor with columns `level` (1 = the employee, increasing toward the top), `name`, and `title`, ordered by level ascending.
sql_schema: CREATE TABLE staff (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, title TEXT, manager_id INTEGER);
sql_setup: INSERT INTO staff VALUES (1, 'CEO', 'Chief', NULL), (2, 'VP1', 'Vice President', 1), (3, 'VP2', 'Vice President', 1), (4, 'EngLead', 'Lead', 2), (5, 'Dev', 'Developer', 4);
reference:
WITH RECURSIVE chain(level, id, name, title, manager_id) AS (
  SELECT 1, id, name, title, manager_id FROM staff s WHERE id = 5
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.level + 1, s.id, s.name, s.title, s.manager_id
  FROM chain c JOIN staff s ON s.id = c.manager_id
)
SELECT level, name, title FROM chain ORDER BY level;
